sections.title: Conquest of Northern Kings
observations: In this section, we see the culmination of Joshua's military campaigns as he faces a coalition of northern kings led by Jabin, the king of Hazor. This coalition represents a significant threat to Israel's possession of the land, as it unites various city-states against them.

The strategy employed by Joshua reflects God's command and guidance. The Lord reassures Joshua not to fear the multitude of enemies, emphasizing that victory is assured because He has delivered them into Israel's hands.
The battle is fierce, but the Lord's intervention is evident. The Israelites are able to rout their enemies, demonstrating the power of God in fulfilling His promises to Israel.

sections.title: Destruction of Hazor and Other Cities
observations: After defeating the northern coalition, Joshua turns his attention to Hazor, the head of the coalition. The complete destruction of Hazor signifies the totality of God's judgment against the Canaanite cities that opposed Israel.
The command to devote these cities to destruction is a reflection of God's holiness and justice. It serves as a warning against the idolatry and wickedness that characterized these nations.
This section also highlights the importance of obedience to God's commands. Joshua's adherence to God's instructions leads to success in the conquest.

importantVerses.commentary: The Lord reassures Joshua not to fear the multitude of enemies, emphasizing His sovereignty and the assurance of victory.
Joshua's obedience to the Lord's commands is highlighted, showing the importance of following God's directives in achieving success.

questions: What does the coalition of northern kings reveal about the opposition Israel faced in their conquest of Canaan?
How does God's reassurance to Joshua in the face of overwhelming odds apply to our lives today?
What can we learn from Joshua's obedience to God's commands in the context of our own spiritual journeys?
